script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 19. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

We call this planet 'Earth,' but it should be called 'Ocean. ' Water covers 71% of the surface and contains 99% of the living space.  Below the waves is an alien world—dark, deep, and full of life we're only beginning to discover.

The ocean contains 321 million cubic miles of water. If you flattened Earth's surface, the ocean would cover the whole planet 2 miles deep. This volume provides 99% of Earth's living space. Land is a thin skin on an ocean world. Even in the deepest trenches—7 miles down, in crushing pressure and total darkness—life thrives.  Creatures we've never imagined, feeding on chemicals from underwater vents or falling debris from above.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: What we don't see can be vast.  The ocean teaches that the invisible world may be larger than the visible.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Ocean Perspective - Appreciate the Unseen.

Here's your activity: Look at a map or globe and notice how much is blue. 71% of the planet, 99% of the living space, 80% unexplored. What creatures might be swimming in the deep right now, never seen by human eyes? The mystery is real and immense. This helps you develop awareness of ocean vastness.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about life under water can be applied to ocean perspective - appreciate the unseen. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
